findings.issue_text: [Critical/bug] In src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71, `organization_context` is never defined anywhere in the endpoint's scope, so `organization_context.member.has_global_access` raises NameError, causing a 500 for every non-superuser GET request.

[High/bug] In src/sentry/api/paginator.py:839, OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key applies math.floor/math.ceil directly to the raw attribute value, which is a datetime object for this endpoint's `order_by="-datetime"`; the datetime→epoch conversion that DateTimePaginator.get_item_key performs was dropped, so building next/prev cursors raises TypeError (500) on any non-empty page.

[High/bug] In src/sentry/api/paginator.py:856, OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result is a verbatim copy of OffsetPaginator's implementation, but the class extends BasePaginator, which does not provide build_queryset/count_hits (or `_is_asc` used by get_item_key), so `self.build_queryset(...)` raises AttributeError; the class must subclass OffsetPaginator (or DateTimePaginator for this endpoint), not BasePaginator.

[High/bug] In src/sentry/api/paginator.py:876-881 (and the prev-cursor path at 182-184), the negative-offset feature assumes `queryset[-N:stop]` slices from the end of the dataset, but Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative bounds (it raises, and negative OFFSET is invalid SQL), so the branch can only produce 500s, never the claimed reverse pagination.

[Medium/bug] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182-184 modifies the shared offset paginator's get_result inherited by nearly every paginated API endpoint: forged forward cursors with negative offsets are silently clamped to offset 0 (serving page-one data instead of rejecting the malformed cursor), while prev cursors still pass negative offsets straight into the ORM — invalid input is half-sanitized and handled inconsistently, and this experiment shouldn't touch shared code at all.

[Medium/security] In src/sentry/api/paginator.py:873-878, `cursor.offset` is unvalidated, forgeable client input (cursors are unsigned base64 JSON) that the new code deliberately turns into data-access behavior beyond normal pagination bounds, justified by the false claim that permissions are checked at the queryset level — but the copied get_result applies post_query_filter/on_results after slicing, so invalid/negative cursor offsets must be rejected at decode time rather than supported.

[Medium/api] In src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:70-90, the same endpoint now produces cursors under two incompatible paginator implementations selected by an undocumented, case-sensitive `optimized_pagination=true` query param combined with user identity; cursors issued by DateTimePaginator are interpreted differently by OptimizedCursorPaginator (and vice versa), so a client following next/prev links across a mode switch silently skips or duplicates rows, and non-privileged users get a silent fallback with no indication of which mode served the response.

[High/test_gap] No tests accompany any of the three changes: the modified shared get_result (affects all paginated endpoints), the new OptimizedCursorPaginator including its enable_advanced_features branches, and the endpoint's new query param/privilege gate; the NameError and paginator crashes would surface in any existing audit-log endpoint test, indicating the new code paths were never executed.

[Medium/doc_defect] Comments added at src/sentry/api/paginator.py:179-181, 852-854, 873-875 and src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:28-29 assert false claims that serve as the PR's justification (e.g., the queryset handles boundary conditions, the Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically, negative offsets enable efficient reverse pagination), which will mislead maintainers into building on broken/unsafe behavior.

[Low/performance] In src/sentry/api/paginator.py:820-912, despite the PR's premise, OptimizedCursorPaginator issues the same filtered/ordered/sliced queries as the existing DateTimePaginator with no index, keyset-pagination, or query-path improvement — just ~90 duplicated lines of get_result and extra branching — leaving the actual cost drivers (datetime ordering, offset scans, counts) untouched and adding risk with no measured benefit.

goldens.comment: The OptimizedCursorPaginator in organization_auditlogs.py attempts to use negative slice offsets on Django querysets, but Django querysets do not support negative slicing and will raise an AssertionError.

When requests are authenticated with API keys or org auth tokens (which have user_id=None), organization_context.member is None. Line 71 attempts to access organization_context.member.has_global_access without checking if member is None, causing an AttributeError crash when optimized_pagination=true is used, even though the request passed all permission checks with valid org:write scope.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` in `organization_auditlogs.py`, but within the shown hunk there is no definition of `organization_context` in the `get()` method prior to its use. If it is not defined elsewhere in the method/file, this would raise a `NameError` at runtime when evaluating the expression (for non-superusers), resulting in a 500.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/bug] In src/sentry/api/paginator.py:856, OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result is a verbatim copy of OffsetPaginator's implementation, but the class extends BasePaginator, which does not provide build_queryset/count_hits (or `_is_asc` used by get_item_key), so `self.build_queryset(...)` raises AttributeError; the class must subclass OffsetPaginator (or DateTimePaginator for this endpoint), not BasePaginator.

adjudication.rationale: The new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` is declared as `class OptimizedCursorPaginator(BasePaginator)` but its implementation calls/uses many attributes and methods it does not define (e.g. `self.build_queryset(...)`, `self.count_hits(...)`, `self._is_asc(...)`, `self.key`, `self.desc`). The diff shows those are not implemented on `OptimizedCursorPaginator` itself, so it is implicitly relying on `BasePaginator` to provide them; if `BasePaginator` is the minimal base (as its name suggests), this will break at runtime when the endpoint selects `paginator_cls=OptimizedCursorPaginator` and `get_result` runs. This strongly indicates the class should subclass the existing paginator that provides those helpers (e.g. the offset/cursor paginator it was copied from), not `BasePaginator`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182-184 modifies the shared offset paginator's get_result inherited by nearly every paginated API endpoint: forged forward cursors with negative offsets are silently clamped to offset 0 (serving page-one data instead of rejecting the malformed cursor), while prev cursors still pass negative offsets straight into the ORM — invalid input is half-sanitized and handled inconsistently, and this experiment shouldn't touch shared code at all.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the shared paginator slicing logic from `queryset[offset:stop]` to `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` and then uses `queryset[start_offset:stop]` (src/sentry/api/paginator.py). This means malformed/forged cursors with a negative `offset` are silently clamped to 0 for forward pagination (serving first-page data), while `cursor.is_prev` continues to pass the raw (potentially negative) `offset` into queryset slicing. That is inconsistent input handling introduced by this change, and can both mask invalid cursors (forward) and still trigger errors (prev) depending on Django's negative-slice behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/security] In src/sentry/api/paginator.py:873-878, `cursor.offset` is unvalidated, forgeable client input (cursors are unsigned base64 JSON) that the new code deliberately turns into data-access behavior beyond normal pagination bounds, justified by the false claim that permissions are checked at the queryset level — but the copied get_result applies post_query_filter/on_results after slicing, so invalid/negative cursor offsets must be rejected at decode time rather than supported.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result()` which (when `enable_advanced_features` is true, as passed from `organization_auditlogs.py`) explicitly allows `cursor.offset < 0` and uses it directly in queryset slicing: `results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])` with `start_offset = cursor.offset` (around new lines ~873-878). `cursor.offset` comes from the decoded cursor (see `Cursor.__init__` in `utils/cursors.py` simply `self.offset = int(offset)` with no validation). This makes client-controlled cursor data influence queryset slicing, and the new behavior intentionally expands to negative offsets. That is risky/incorrect: Django QuerySet slicing does not generally support negative indices (can raise), and even aside from exceptions, this is “data-access behavior beyond normal pagination bounds” driven by untrusted input. The claim in comments about safety/permissions is not enforced in this code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/api] In src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:70-90, the same endpoint now produces cursors under two incompatible paginator implementations selected by an undocumented, case-sensitive `optimized_pagination=true` query param combined with user identity; cursors issued by DateTimePaginator are interpreted differently by OptimizedCursorPaginator (and vice versa), so a client following next/prev links across a mode switch silently skips or duplicates rows, and non-privileged users get a silent fallback with no indication of which mode served the response.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly introduces two pagination modes in the same endpoint selected by a case-sensitive `optimized_pagination=="true"` flag plus an authorization check (`is_superuser` or `has_global_access`), with a silent fallback to `DateTimePaginator` when not authorized (no header/field indicating which paginator was used). However, the claim that cursors are "incompatible" and will necessarily skip/duplicate rows across mode switches is not directly verifiable from the diff because the cursor encoding/Link generation behavior of `self.paginate` and `DateTimePaginator` is not shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/test_gap] No tests accompany any of the three changes: the modified shared get_result (affects all paginated endpoints), the new OptimizedCursorPaginator including its enable_advanced_features branches, and the endpoint's new query param/privilege gate; the NameError and paginator crashes would surface in any existing audit-log endpoint test, indicating the new code paths were never executed.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds and changes nontrivial pagination logic in three places (organization endpoint gate on `optimized_pagination`/admin access, shared `get_result` slice behavior, and an entirely new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with an `enable_advanced_features` branch), but the PR diff contains no accompanying test changes or additions. While we can’t prove from the diff alone that existing tests would fail or that specific runtime errors occur, the absence of tests for these new/changed code paths is a concrete, diff-grounded review concern rather than a direct defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/doc_defect] Comments added at src/sentry/api/paginator.py:179-181, 852-854, 873-875 and src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:28-29 assert false claims that serve as the PR's justification (e.g., the queryset handles boundary conditions, the Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically, negative offsets enable efficient reverse pagination), which will mislead maintainers into building on broken/unsafe behavior.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces/endorses negative queryset slicing, which Django QuerySets do not support. In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, when `enable_advanced_features` and `cursor.offset < 0`, it does `results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])` with `start_offset` negative. Similarly, the modified paginator logic uses `start_offset = ... if not cursor.is_prev else offset`, so `offset` can be negative for prev cursors, again leading to `queryset[offset:stop]`. Django raises errors on negative indexing/slicing, so the comments claiming the ORM “properly handles negative slicing automatically” and that this is “safe” are misleading and the code path is broken.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/performance] In src/sentry/api/paginator.py:820-912, despite the PR's premise, OptimizedCursorPaginator issues the same filtered/ordered/sliced queries as the existing DateTimePaginator with no index, keyset-pagination, or query-path improvement — just ~90 duplicated lines of get_result and extra branching — leaving the actual cost drivers (datetime ordering, offset scans, counts) untouched and adding risk with no measured benefit.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `OptimizedCursorPaginator` largely duplicating an existing cursor paginator `get_result` implementation (new class in `src/sentry/api/paginator.py` adds ~90 lines with similar `build_queryset(...)`, hit counting, and Django slicing `queryset[start_offset:stop]`). The only substantive change appears to be conditional handling of negative offsets when `enable_advanced_features` is set, plus additional branching/flags in `organization_auditlogs.py`. There is no diff-visible change to indexing, ordering strategy, or query construction beyond that, so the reviewer’s point that this adds complexity without an obvious, diff-grounded query-path improvement is a valid non-bug concern (though claims about “no index”/exact cost drivers can’t be proven from the diff alone).
